Marissa / team / John,

I reviewed Acmes redlines and drafted suggested edits. High-level points and recommended language below (summary):

1) Role clarity: Use "service provider" (CCPA) and "processor" (CPRA/other US states) consistently. Avoid ambiguous terms like "contractor" without defined privacy role.
2) Sale vs Sharing: CPRA expands "sharing" beyond traditional "sale." We should accept language that affirms Redwood does not "sell or share" personal information for purposes outside the contract, but propose a carve for machine-learning model improvements using deidentified/aggregated telemetry if Acme approves.
3) Subprocessors: Add a clause that Redwood will provide an up-to-date list at https://status.redwood.com/subprocessors and will provide 30 days' notice via email before onboarding a new subprocessor. Objection process: Acme can object on reasonable security/privacy grounds; if unresolved, Redwood will offer mitigation or an exit window (45 days).

4) Data transfers & cross-border: Default: data stored/processed in customer-selected region. If Redwood conducts incidental cross-border processing for infrastructure reasons, include appropriate safeguards. If Acme requires EU-only residency, add region-specific SOW.

5) Deletion & backups: We recommend accepting the 90-day backup exception but add a requirement that backups will be encrypted and deletion requests will be honored in primary stores within 30 days; backups will be logically deleted within 90 days except to the extent legal holds apply.

6) Audit / SOC 2 evidence: Offer SOC 2 Type II report annually and allow a remote security questionnaire response and up to one on-site audit per year with notice and NDA.

7) Indemnity / liability: Keep commercial caps consistent with master services agreement; do not accept open-ended liability for state statutory penalties without carveouts.

I attached a redline PDF with inline comments: "Redwood-Redlines-20260211.pdf". Specific drafting suggestions are in the PDF; notable redlines include a CPRA "sharing" definition and a clear subprocessor notification cadence.

Once Acme reviews these changes and confirms the region/residency requirements, we can prepare a finalized addendum for signatures. Id also like a short call to walk through the non-standard items (sharing carve, subprocessor objection).

Evelyn Hart
Sr. Counsel, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference
